data.title: Guinea-Bissau junta urges military unit loyal to ex-president to disarm
data.description: BISSAU - Guinea-Bissau's junta leader General Horta N'Tam urged members of the presidential guard loyal to exiled former president Umaro Sissoco Embalo to voluntarily lay down their weapons on Wednesday.

data.title: As species decline, green turtles offer glimmer of hope
data.description: MATAKING (MALAYSIA) - The palm-sized green turtle hatchling flailing through the sand on a Malaysian island may seem vulnerable, but its species has emerged as a symbol of hope for wildlife conservation.

data.title: Five priorities to avert a property crisis: unlocking home loans and tackling global warming
data.description: Three property associations have identified five major challenges in reviving the market through action by the government and banks.

data.title: Hell's Kitchen Thailand is back and waiting on your reservation
data.description: The kitchen is on fire again and this time the pressure multiplies as Hell's Kitchen Thailand is back for the third season.

data.title: What to pack in your travel first-aid kit
data.description: The gentleman who'd gotten off the train ahead of me collapsed, his eyebrow splitting open as he hit the concrete. Blood dripped onto his suit. His wife gasped. "I'm supposed to be going to the theatre," he mumbled.

data.title: Get spiritual  with 'Fortune Teller' at  One Bangkok
data.description: One Bangkok invites everyone to play, explore and initiate a personal dialogue with nature during "Fortune Teller", which is running on the 2nd floor of The Storeys, Rama IV Road, daily from 10am to 8pm until Nov 15.

data.title: Connecting Thailand and Taiwan for 35 years
data.description: When EVA Air began operating between Bangkok and Taipei in 1991, the airline was still in its early years. Founded in 1989 as Taiwan's first privately owned international airline, EVA Air was then in the early stages of developing its international route network.

data.description: The day of the week you were born on can reveal a lot... Read on.

data.title: 'The Mall Lifestore Taste Of J'  kicks off Vegetarian Festival 2026
data.description: The Mall Group celebrates the Vegetarian Festival 2026 with the return of "The Mall Lifestore Taste Of J" featuring more than 3,000 dishes from four of Thailand's renowned vegetarian food destinations.

data.title: Hudson sticks with beaten Thai stars
data.description: Anthony Hudson intends to keep faith with the core of the squad that fell just short in the Fifa Asean Cup, as Thailand's head coach turns his attention to next year's Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia.

data.title: Saysunee gunning for trio of gold
data.description: Five-time Paralympic gold medallist Saysunee Jana will lead the Thai wheelchair fencing team at the 2026 Asian Para Games, while the coaching staff have identified China and South Korea as their key rivals in Aichi-Nagoya from Oct 18-24.

data.title: Bangkok faces submersion risk
data.description: Bangkok could have as much as one-third of its area permanently submerged by 2050 if the government fails to overhaul the country's water-management system and take more aggressive action on climate change, environmental and water-management experts warned at a forum.

data.title: Chula launches new centre
data.description: Chulalongkorn University's Faculty of Engineering has launched a Water Resilience Centre to help Thailand prepare for extreme flooding under a "Black Swan" scenario in which multiple threats strike simultaneously.

data.title: PP rejects 'entertainocracy' tag, insists unity intact
data.description: People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut insists the party remains united despite criticism from former Future Forward Party (FFP) secretary-general Piyabutr Saengkanokkul over what he calls the rise of "entertainocracy" in politics.

data.title: ThaiHealth funding debate heats up
data.description: The government's plan to end ThaiHealth's earmarked alcohol and tobacco tax funding of more than 4 billion baht a year has drawn mixed views over fiscal scrutiny, independence and public health.

data.title: Close the gap in HIV treatment: UN
data.description: The Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/Aids (UNAIDS) has called for governments, communities, businesses and other sectors to work together to close gaps in HIV prevention and treatment across the Asia-Pacific region.

data.title: BJT MP challenges committee boss
data.description: Bhumjaithai Party (BJT) MP Suphachai Jaismut on Wednesday challenged House committee chairman Rangsiman Rome's authority to place allegations against fellow BJT MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap and her husband on the committee's agenda.

data.title: 2 Myanmar women, 1 Chinese held over B200m scam
data.description: Police have arrested a Chinese man and two Myanmar women over an alleged call-centre network accused of defrauding at least seven students of more than 200 million baht.

data.title: Skydivers fly Thai flag in record attempt
data.description: One Flag Thailand has completed its first world-record mission, flying a 4,303-square-foot Thai national flag over Pattaya.

data.title: Court rejects NBTC chief's B20m suit for defamation
data.description: A civil court has dismissed a 20-million-baht lawsuit filed by National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission (NBTC) chairman Dr Sarana Boonbaichaiyapruck against four fellow commissioners, ruling their criticisms concerned their official duties and served the public interest.

data.title: Nene to perform at IMF dinner
data.description: Nene Royal, the 16-year-old Thai winner of America's Got Talent, will perform at a state dinner hosted by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul for 400 global leaders attending the IMF-World Bank meetings at Government House on Oct 14.

data.title: IP-backed financing will drive Thai creative content
data.description: The Creative Economy Agency (Public Organization), or CEA, is shifting its focus towards creative content as a crucial strategic pillar of economic growth across Asean.

data.title: Govt moves to protect meet
data.description: The government has developed a business continuity plan to ensure the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings run smoothly, even if heavy rainfall mars the global gathering, said Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas.

data.title: Russia's plague scare: What we know
data.description: MOSCOW - The death of a plague laboratory worker in Siberia last week has made global headlines, with Russian media suggesting hundreds were under quarantine and US President Donald Trump expressing concern.

data.title: Russia warns of 'false' information as second plague case reported
data.description: MOSCOW - Russia warned Wednesday against "false" information as reports emerged of a second suspected case of plague in Siberia, with Washington and Brussels calling for transparency and neighbouring Mongolia tightening health surveillance.

data.title: Thousands march fearing return of a Bolsonaro presidency in Brazil
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - Thousands of people joined a student march Wednesday in downtown Rio de Janeiro to protest presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and a surge of the far-right in Brazil.

data.title: Trump says 'we don't think' Russian plague is bio-weapon
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that the death of a Russian plague laboratory worker did not appear to be linked to a biological weapon.

data.title: WHO says cannot conduct full risk assessment on Russia plague reports
data.description: GENEVA - The World Health Organization said Wednesday it could not produce a full risk assessment as it did not have the whole picture from Russia on the suspected plague death of a laboratory technician.

data.title: German Chancellor marks October 7 with vow to fight antisemitism
data.description: BERLIN - Chancellor Friedrich Merz marked the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel by vowing to fight antisemitism in Germany while pressing for a two-state solution in the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

data.title: Spared, married, hanged: an Iranian protester’s last weeks
data.description: Alireza Sepahi was arrested in the wake of Iran’s January protests, was spared public execution in July after suffering a heart attack and married his fiancee on the eve of his death.

data.title: German ex-spy chief kept in jail after treason arrest
data.description: BERLIN - A court Wednesday ordered former German spy chief August Hanning to remain in jail after his arrest on suspicion of espionage and treason, along with a former deputy who allegedly supplied him with secret files.

data.title: Heavy casualties in Ukraine after Russian strikes
data.description: PRYLUKY, Ukraine - At least 20 people were killed in Russian strikes across Ukraine on Wednesday, including 14 when a missile slammed into an apartment block in the north of the country as they slept.

data.title: Thaksin appears in court to challenge asset seizure
data.description: Former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra told a court on Wednesday that the seizure and freezing of his assets to recover a 17.6-billion-baht tax debt were unlawful, arguing that poor coordination between the Revenue Department and the Ministry of Finance had led to him being pursued twice for the same debt.

data.title: Care home that ‘caged’ residents to be shut down
data.description: Health authorities are preparing to shut down an elderly care centre in Kanchanaburi after finding multiple violations, including providing services beyond the scope of its licence, including having caged beds, illegal expansion and admitting mentally ill patients.

data.title: French-Japanese duo win Nobel chemistry prize
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Henri Kagan of France and Kenso Soai of Japan have been awarded the Nobel chemistry prize for solving the mystery of why only one version of some molecules’ mirror-image forms appears in nature, a discovery decisive for the development of pharmaceuticals.

data.title: PM Anutin wants water retention areas around Bangkok
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning to study ways to develop water retention areas around Bangkok in order to prevent future floods.
